audit.description: Changed production code in OpenSeries/util/constant.py replaces `from colorama import Fore, Style` with `from rich.color import Color` and computes the red ANSI escape through `Color.parse('red').get_ansi_codes()`, which is meaningful target-library use. The static and dynamic anti-cheat evidence report no source-library imports or namespace access from changed production code, while dynamic target events originate from the installed rich package in site-packages with target_local_spec_count 0, so there is no evidence of a fake local provider.
evidence: Unified diff: OpenSeries/util/constant.py changes `from colorama import Fore, Style` to `from rich.color import Color` and uses `Color.parse('red').get_ansi_codes()` for `red`.
Static anti-cheat: OpenSeries/util/constant.py has imports_target=true, imports_source=false, source_namespace_access=false, fake_target_added_code=false, target_provider_added=false.
Dynamic anti-cheat: first target import is module `rich.color` from OpenSeries/util/constant.py line 1 with origin under after_venv_overlay site-packages/rich/__init__.py.
Dependency files replace colorama with rich in requirements.txt, dev-requirements.txt, OpenSeriesBellshade.egg-info/requires.txt, and PKG-INFO.
reasons: Production code imports and uses rich.color.Color.
Changed production code no longer imports colorama.
Dynamic evidence shows rich events from production code and no colorama import attempts.
No local fake rich provider was detected.
